title: Backup, Restore, and Clean Up Volumes
description: Back up a volume to a tar file, delete the volume, restore it, and verify data integrity.
problemStatement:
## Objective
Learn to back up a Docker volume to your host, delete the volume, and restore it from the backup.

### Steps
1. Create a volume named `db-data`.
2. Add some files to it by running a container:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm -v db-data:/data alpine sh -c 'echo "file1" > /data/f1.txt && echo "file2" > /data/f2.txt'
   ```
3. Back up the volume to a tar file in your current directory:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm -v db-data:/data -v $(pwd):/backup alpine tar czf /backup/db-data.tar.gz -C /data .
   ```
4. Delete the original volume:
   ```bash
   docker volume rm db-data
   ```
5. Create a new volume (same name or different) `db-data-restored`.
6. Restore the backup into the new volume:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm -v db-data-restored:/data -v $(pwd):/backup alpine tar xzf /backup/db-data.tar.gz -C /data
   ```
7. Verify the files are restored:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm -v db-data-restored:/data alpine ls /data
   docker run --rm -v db-data-restored:/data alpine cat /data/f1.txt
   ```
8. Clean up the backup file and volume:
   ```bash
   rm db-data.tar.gz
   docker volume rm db-data-restored
   ```

### Deliverable
Terminal output showing the backup file creation, volume removal, and successful file listing after restore.
hints: The `$(pwd)` substitutes the current directory. Ensure you have write permissions there.
If `tar` fails, check that the volume name is correct and that the volume contains files.
expectedOutput: The restored volume shows f1.txt and f2.txt, and their content matches the original.
solutionCode:
docker volume create db-data
docker run --rm -v db-data:/data alpine sh -c 'echo "file1" > /data/f1.txt && echo "file2" > /data/f2.txt'
docker run --rm -v db-data:/data -v $(pwd):/backup alpine tar czf /backup/db-data.tar.gz -C /data .
docker volume rm db-data
docker volume create db-data-restored
docker run --rm -v db-data-restored:/data -v $(pwd):/backup alpine tar xzf /backup/db-data.tar.gz -C /data
docker run --rm -v db-data-restored:/data alpine ls /data
docker run --rm -v db-data-restored:/data alpine cat /data/f1.txt
rm db-data.tar.gz
docker volume rm db-data-restored
